name: Tsentar
tagline: The pedestrian centre, opening onto the Sea Garden
description: Burgas's core runs along the pedestrianised Aleksandrovska and ends at the Sea Garden, the long clifftop park above the beach. Restored facades, cafes, the opera house and the main shopping all sit here, and the walk from a flat to the sea takes a couple of minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the park, the beach and the restaurants all on foot
pros: Sea Garden and beach a few minutes away
All restaurants, cafes and services within walking distance
Fast fibre and the best connectivity in the city
cons: Highest rents in Burgas, and they rise in summer
Busy and noisy through the season

name: Lazur
tagline: Between the centre and the beach, residential and close in
description: A residential district immediately north of the centre, running behind the Sea Garden towards the beach. Mid-rise blocks, local shops and a short walk to both the park and the pedestrian street. It is one of the more sought-after everyday districts precisely because of that position.
bestFor: Longer stays that want the sea close without paying centre prices
pros: Five to ten minutes on foot to the Sea Garden
Cheaper than the centre for a similar flat
cons: Blocks are plain and some are dated
Summer traffic on the routes to the beach

name: Izgrev
tagline: Established estates, good value and well connected
description: A large residential district northwest of the centre with supermarkets, a market, schools and frequent buses. The flats are typical Bulgarian panel and brick blocks, larger and cheaper than anything nearer the sea, and the lakes on the western side are within reach for walking.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space and a low rent with a bus into town
pros: Considerably cheaper than the coastal districts
Full everyday shopping and a local market
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes from the sea
Nothing much happening in the evening

name: Slaveykov
tagline: The largest estate district, cheapest rents in the city
description: Burgas's biggest residential complex, built to the northwest with its own commercial centre, markets and schools. It is entirely unglamorous, well served by buses and by some distance the cheapest place in the city to rent a decent flat. Lake Vaya sits on its western side with birdwatching hides.
bestFor: The tightest budgets, with the lake rather than the sea as the local walk
pros: Its own shops, markets and services
Lake Vaya and its birdlife on the western edge
cons: Little reason to be here other than the price

name: Sarafovo
tagline: A former fishing village on the beach, north past the airport
description: A separate settlement on the coast about eight kilometres north, with its own long sandy beach, a small harbour and a village atmosphere that the city proper has lost. It sits beside the airport, which is both convenient and audible. Buses run into Burgas regularly along the bay.
bestFor: Quiet coastal stays with a beach at the door and the city half an hour away
pros: Long, uncrowded beach directly below the village
cons: Twenty-five to thirty minutes by bus to the city centre
Very quiet and partly shuttered out of season
